idiom_name: per-route handler function + separate response builder over libmicrohttpd
implementation_notes: C has no HTTP stack in its standard library, so the router and the response builder are both hand-written: a static table maps method plus path to a handler function, the handler receives url/method/upload data through MHD_AccessHandlerCallback, converts what it needs into plain values, calls the domain, and a separate responder function queues status, headers and body with MHD_queue_response. The classic three-object split collapses to two families of functions (actions and responders) over a small request struct because C has no classes - that is still ADR as long as the domain entry point never receives the MHD_Connection or the request struct. Keep the split when one action must produce several representations or when the domain must stay callable from a CLI or an embedded system without the HTTP stack at all.
pitfalls: con_cls is per HTTP request, not per connection: state stored there must be freed by the MHD_OPTION_NOTIFY_COMPLETED callback or it leaks.
Returning MHD_NO aborts the request; a handler that returns MHD_NO after queueing a response silently drops it.
Handlers run on the daemon's threads, so any shared domain state (caches, counters, connection pools) must be locked or thread-confined.
